aboutH2: Village of Hope Eston: Faith-Based Residential Recovery in Eston, SK
intro: Village of Hope Eston is a Christian residential program for adults with drug and alcohol addictions, on the former Eston College campus in west-central Saskatchewan. The centre calls it a ten-month regeneration program. Its program pages and recent local news describe it as a program for men, and students live on campus for the whole stay.

Mornings are for classes and afternoons are for work, much of it in the Village of Hope bakery or on landscaping and off-site crews. The program asks a $1,200 income-based entrance fee and helps students apply for government benefits to cover monthly costs. Donors and the centre's own small businesses pay for the rest.

pillars.title: A College Campus in a Prairie Town
pillars.body: Village of Hope runs on the old Eston College campus at 730 1st Street East, a few blocks from the centre of Eston. The college gave the campus to the ministry, and local news describes dormitories, classrooms and a working bakery on site. Eston is a small farm town in west-central Saskatchewan, surrounded by wheat fields, about 45 minutes from Kindersley and under three hours from Saskatoon. The centre likes to point out that it is far from the noise and pace of the city, and there are no trips to town or weekends off during the program.

pillars.title: Five Phases over Ten Months
pillars.body: The program starts with a four-week introduction to the program and to Christian living. Orientation follows, where students look at what addiction has done to their relationships and take part in the Sociogram, a group exercise in honest feedback. In Regeneration they learn the physical and psychological effects of addiction through Biblical counselling, classes and small groups. Inner Healing works on root issues such as childhood abuse and rejection, and Discipleship shifts the focus to faith and serving others. Students work through four classroom workbooks along the way.

pillars.title: A Bakery, Work Crews and a Full Day
pillars.body: Afternoons are for work. Students bake cinnamon buns, bread and cheese sticks for the Village of Hope bakery, which opens to the public after morning classes, and they go out on landscaping jobs and off-site work for local people and companies. The day starts at 6am and ends with evening activities such as sports, study, prayer meetings or a movie. Graduates who want to work in addictions can apply for Servant Leader Training, a further year of classes and supervised work with a staff mentor.

overviewH2: Village of Hope Eston: Who It Is For and How It Is Funded
overview: The curriculum is for adults 18 and over who want to deal with a drug or alcohol problem inside a Christian program. Applicants call the office first, read the guidelines, send an application and then have an in-person interview with the program director. The centre says the interview is not automatic acceptance and is used to judge whether someone is ready.

afterOverview: Village of Hope Eston does not offer detox, outpatient care or a licensed clinical team, and it does not list provincial licensing or accreditation. Counselling is Biblical, and the program asks students to give up phones, TV and the internet for the length of the stay. Men who want a faith-based program with a long stay and real work every day may find that a good fit. Anyone needing medical withdrawal care or a secular program should look at other Saskatchewan options too.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What kind of program is Village of Hope Eston?
faqs.a: Village of Hope Eston is a Christian residential recovery program for adults with drug and alcohol problems, run on a campus in Eston, Saskatchewan. Students live on site for about 10 months and work through classes on orientation, regeneration, inner healing and discipleship, alongside daily work. The centre calls itself a regeneration program and uses Biblical counselling, classroom teaching and small groups.

faqs.q: Is the program for men or women?
faqs.a: The program pages, the recovery.com profile and 2025 local news coverage all describe a program for men. The home page of the centre's website mentions men and women, so call 306-962-3000 to confirm whether women are accepted at the Eston campus.

faqs.q: How much does Village of Hope Eston cost?
faqs.a: There is a $1,200 entrance fee, which the centre says is income-based and non-refundable. Staff help each student apply for government support such as EI sickness benefits or social assistance to cover monthly costs. The rest of the program is paid for by donations, fundraising and the centre's own social enterprises.

The program runs about 10 months, and sometimes up to a year depending on the person. Graduates who feel called to work in addictions can stay for a further year in the Servant Leader Training program.

faqs.q: Does Village of Hope Eston offer detox?
faqs.a: No. The centre's website does not describe a detox or medical withdrawal service, and recovery.com lists detox as not offered. Medications are handed over at intake and given out under staff direction, so talk to your doctor and the intake team about withdrawal care before you arrive.

faqs.q: Where is Village of Hope Eston?
faqs.a: The campus is at 730 1st Street East in Eston, a small town in west-central Saskatchewan. It is about 2 hours 45 minutes from Saskatoon and about 3.5 hours from Regina, and Kindersley is around 45 minutes away. The mailing address is P.O. Box 490, Eston, SK S0L 1A0.

faqs.q: What does a typical day look like?
faqs.a: Students are up at 6am, eat breakfast at 6:30 and spend 7am on chores, devotions and journaling. Classes run from 8 to 10:30am, followed by work until supper at 5:30pm. Evenings have sports, study, prayer meetings, worship and movie nights, with the odd outing off campus.

faqs.q: What are the rules during the program?
faqs.a: Tobacco is not allowed, and having drugs or alcohol means immediate dismissal. Students do not use TV, radio or the internet, phone calls are limited to emergencies, and there are no trips to town or weekends off during the 10 months. Letter writing is encouraged as a way to rebuild family ties.

Yes, after the first three weeks. Visitors must be on the approved list and attend an orientation class first. Visits are Sunday from 2pm to 5pm, or families can come for the 11am church service and stay for a meal, and the office asks you to call by 5pm on Wednesday.

faqs.q: What work training is part of the program?
faqs.a: Students work in the Village of Hope bakery, which is open to the public, and on landscaping and off-site work crews that local people can hire. The centre says this gives real work experience and helps raise money for the program.

Call 306-962-3000 for an intake call first; the centre does not accept collect calls. Then read the program guidelines, fill in the application online or on paper, and email it to estonvillageofhope@gmail.com. The last step is an in-person interview with the program director, booked on a weekday between 8am and 5pm.
